pOne: Filtering is happening at all stages in the EEG process. From the time you begin recording an EEG, you or the manufacturer should have already set up some parameters that disclose your frequency range of interest. Typically, you want to get all the frequencies as close to 0 Hz as possible and can capture frequencies up to half your sampling rate, which is known as your nyquist frequency.
pTwo: The most simple kind of filter you can make is a bandpass filter. This will specify the lowest frequencies and the highest ones you want to capture. In most cases, we cut off at 0.1 or 1 Hz to reduce repeating noise around the Delta frequency bands. At the higher end of the spectrum, we cut off at 40 Hz. Frequencies above this are less likely to be associated with brain activity.
pThree: A notch filter is a filter to remove power line noise. In certain countries it is 50 Hz and in America it is 60 Hz. Conveniently, the Emotiv headset already has this filter built into the equipment and software. There should be no reason to manually set this, but you can if you want to.
